record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let p in C[x_1, ..., x_n] define a contractible hypersurface X={p=0} in C^n. Must p be isotrivial, meaning that its generic fibers are pairwise isomorphic hypersurfaces?

evidence.quote: 2.2. QUESTION. Let p ∈ C[x1, . . . , x n] be such that the hypersurface X = {p = 0} in Cn is contractible. Is then p an isotrivial polynomial, i.e. such that its generic ﬁbres are pairwise isomorphic hypersurfaces in Cn ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 2$ and let $p\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial such that the hypersurface $X=\{p=0\}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is contractible (as a topological space with its classical topology). Call $p$ isotrivial if there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that for all $c_1,c_2\in U$ the fibers $\{p=c_1\}$ and $\{p=c_2\}$ are isomorphic as algebraic hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Question: Must every such polynomial $p$ (whose zero fiber defines a contractible hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^n$) be isotrivial?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related work by Kaliman, Makar-Limanov, and Zaidenberg on contractible affine hypersurfaces and exotic $\mathbb{C}^3$ structures, but no source explicitly resolves the isotriviality question for arbitrary polynomials whose zero hypersurface is contractible in $\mathbb{C}^n$. The status appears not to be definitively settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Smooth contractible hypersurfaces in C^n and exotic algebraic structures on C^3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies contractible hypersurfaces in C^n and exotic structures on C^3 but does not state a general isotriviality theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on contractible hypersurfaces exist but do not directly settle the isotriviality question.

status_evidence.title: AK-invariant of affine domains (Kaliman-Makar-Limanov)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses contractible hypersurfaces X_{m,n,k,l} in C^4 and computes Makar-Limanov invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Work on contractible hypersurfaces continues but no decisive answer to the general isotriviality question is given.
